title: An OpenCode seat waits five minutes on every stalled provider call
foundBy: repository owner, from a task-tracker campaign whose modeller lost most of a lap to provider stalls
details:
OpenCode waits 300 seconds for a provider's response headers before it gives up on a call. It then retries the call silently, up to six attempts with backoff, so one stuck call costs about 31 minutes before the turn ends and the campaign resumes the seat. In a task-tracker campaign, a modeller on glm-5p3 at Fireworks lost about 85 of 92 minutes this way, to 24 header timeouts. Other seats on the same machine were healthy. The seat read plain `busy` throughout. The modeller's slowest genuine call over three stores took 34.6 seconds to start answering, and the median was 1.0 to 1.4 seconds.

OpenCode reads the wait from `provider.<id>.options.headerTimeout`, in milliseconds. A profile has no way to set it. Wanted: a per-seat number, in seconds, that the campaign writes there for an OpenCode seat. A seat without it must run exactly as it does now. A seat on another CLI must be refused rather than have the number ignored.
